name: Ask About a Detail
form: Choose a detail, ask AI about it, then write what you think.
short: Choose a detail, ask AI about it, then write what you think.

steps.title: Choose and ask
steps.human: Choose a point on the object photo and write one question. Record your first view before seeing AI.
steps.example: Why does this jug look as if it is wearing clothes?
steps.data: Selected point, question and first view.

steps.title: Read one answer
steps.human: Read a short answer and open its source if you wish. Keep the chosen detail on screen.
steps.example: The source calls this a leather jug shaped like a dressed woman. It is not evidence that the collar is cloth.
steps.ai: Use the photo, question and fixed museum fact card; say when the card does not answer the question.
steps.data: Exact answer, source version and whether the source was opened.

steps.title: Write your view
steps.human: Keep your first view, change it, or leave the question open; add a reason in your own words.
steps.example: I now see shaped leather, but I still wonder why the maker chose clothing.
steps.data: Final view and reason, including disagreement or no change.

case: Cleveland Museum of Art: Look Closer / Talk to the Art
caseFact: Look Closer supports close looking through AR; Talk to the Art answers visitor questions using museum material. AR alone is not generative AI.
invite: Choose a point on the object photo and write one question. Record your first view before seeing AI.
followup: What, if anything, made you feel closer to or further from this object? What led you to that view?
build: A photo viewer, point selection, one sourced AI answer and a saved final note.

name: Make a Shape
form: Make a shape with cloth or paper, photograph it, and tell AI what it missed about making it.
short: Make a shape with cloth or paper, photograph it, and tell AI what it missed about making it.

steps.title: Make and feel
steps.human: Fold ordinary cloth or paper into a shape inspired by the jug’s collar. Note how it feels to make it.
steps.example: The folds spring back when I let go.
steps.data: Material choice, first idea and words about touch.

steps.title: Show your shape
steps.human: Take one tabletop photo, check the crop and send it with your note. Read one comparison with the object detail.
steps.example: The folds look similar, but this photo cannot show their weight or stiffness.
steps.ai: Compare visible shapes and quote the visitor’s own account of touch. Do not claim to feel the material.
steps.data: Confirmed photo, note, source image and full AI response.

steps.title: Say what AI missed
steps.human: Mark one useful point and one thing the comparison missed; explain whether making changed your link to the object.
steps.example: It saw the folds, but not how hard it was to hold the shape.
steps.data: Visitor corrections, reasons and final account.
steps.controls: Keep a point / Add what is missing

case: Cleveland Museum of Art: Art Morph
caseFact: Art Morph uses a camera to turn arrangements of everyday materials into AI images.
invite: Fold ordinary cloth or paper into a shape inspired by the jug’s collar. Note how it feels to make it.
followup: What did your hands tell you that the picture did not? Did that affect your connection with the object?
build: A photo preview and crop, one image-and-text request, and editable notes.

name: Change One Detail
form: Ask AI to change one detail in an object photo, then decide whether the result still feels connected to the object.
short: Ask AI to change one detail in an object photo, then decide whether the result still feels connected to the object.

steps.title: Set the change
steps.human: On a digital photo, mark one small area to change and name something that must stay.
steps.example: Change one bird’s colour; keep its shape and the rest of the pane.
steps.data: Original image, marked area, change request and keep rule.

steps.title: Compare two images
steps.human: View the original next to one AI edit. The original remains clearly labelled and available.
steps.example: Original object photo / New AI image
steps.ai: Generate within the marked area; the app restores all pixels outside it from the original.
steps.data: Prompt, mask, original image and generated image.

steps.title: Decide what it means
steps.human: Keep, reject or set aside the edit; say what still links it to the object and what has changed.
steps.example: It is my version of the bird, not evidence of how the old glass looked.
steps.data: Decision, unchanged features that matter and reason.

case: Cleveland Museum of Art: Extend the Art
caseFact: Extend the Art lets visitors use AI to extend an image beyond its frame.
invite: On a digital photo, mark one small area to change and name something that must stay.
followup: Which part must stay for this image to keep a meaningful link to the object, and why?
build: A mask editor, one image-edit request, pixel restoration outside the mask and side-by-side views.

name: Write a Label Together
form: Write one line each about an object, let AI combine them, then decide what the shared label should say.
short: Write one line each about an object, let AI combine them, then decide what the shared label should say.

steps.title: Write separately
steps.human: Each person writes one line before seeing the other person’s words. Then reveal both.
steps.example: A: I notice the care in the folds. B: I wonder who used it.
steps.data: Separate texts from A and B, linked to the same object.

steps.title: Read a shared draft
steps.human: Read one short AI label next to both original lines and the museum fact card.
steps.example: We notice both the made detail and the question of who used this object.
steps.ai: Combine the two views without adding history or turning one person’s view into a fact.
steps.data: Exact draft and the source texts it used.

steps.title: Keep both voices
steps.human: Each person marks words to keep or change; edit the label together or leave two different labels.
steps.example: Keep “care”, but do not say we both feel the same thing.
steps.ai: No further call; final changes are made by people.
steps.data: Each person’s edits, discussion and final choice.

case: Nasher Museum of Art: Act as if you are a curator
caseFact: The museum used AI in exhibition planning and text writing. This was a curatorial project, not a two-visitor label activity.
invite: Each person writes one line before seeing the other person’s words. Then reveal both.
followup: Which words still feel like yours? Does sharing this label change your connection with the object?
build: Two separate text fields, one AI draft, a shared text editor and separate choices.

name: Share a Detail
form: Choose an object detail for a friend, let AI help word your message, then see how your friend responds.
short: Choose an object detail for a friend, let AI help word your message, then see how your friend responds.

steps.title: Choose for someone
steps.human: Choose a detail and write why this person came to mind. Keep the first message.
steps.example: This pattern made me think of the cloth you keep at home.
steps.data: Detail, first message and sender’s reason.

steps.title: Choose your words
steps.human: Read one AI rewrite. Use it, edit it yourself, or keep your own message. Pass the tablet to your friend.
steps.example: Look closely at this pattern. Does it remind you of anything we have seen together?
steps.ai: Rewrite the message in up to 40 words; invent no shared memory or object history.
steps.data: AI draft, sender’s selected text and reason for the choice.

steps.title: Hear the reply
steps.human: The friend sees the detail and message, responds, then both compare the first message, AI draft and chosen version.
steps.example: I thought of a different cloth, but I understood why you sent it.
steps.data: Recipient response and both people’s account of the connection.

caseFact: GIFT invites visitors to choose museum objects and create personal gifts using photos and voice messages. It is not a generative AI project.
invite: Choose a detail and write why this person came to mind. Keep the first message.
followup: What reached the recipient, and what changed along the way? Where did the personal connection come from?
build: A detail picker, three saved text versions and a hand-over screen for the reply.
